heroHeadline: 3 SAC Columns Advance on Maw Taung as Lay Kay Falls; 8,000+ Displaced in Pauk; 820+ Chin Civilians Flee to India; IIMM Marks 1-Year Oe Htein Kwin School Massacre Anniversary
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,930 of Myanmar's civil war (May 16, 2026), the junta escalated on multiple fronts: three SAC columns pushed toward Maw Taung — KNLA Brigade 4's key Thailand border town in Tanintharyi — conducting daily airstrikes as they advanced to within 15 miles of the crossing, while Lay Kay camp in KNLA Brigade 1 territory (Bilin Township, Mon State) fell on May 11 after the SAC deployed drones, paramotors, and aircraft. In Magway Region, the junta's offensive through Pauk Township has displaced approximately 8,000 residents from 14 villages since May 1 — major escalation occurred May 11 with heavy artillery, drone strikes, and airstrikes — adding to 24,000 already displaced from 52 villages; Saw Town was occupied and 20+ young men arrested. The humanitarian crisis in Chin State deepened further: 820+ civilians fled to India's Mizoram between May 11-13 from Tedim Township, Tonzang, and the Falam-Hakha road region as reports emerged of an impending junta offensive on Rikhawdar — the last India-Myanmar trade border town held by Chin resistance. In a major accountability development, the UN's Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar (IIMM) marked the first anniversary of the May 12, 2025 Oe Htein Kwin village school massacre (20+ students killed) with data showing 640+ airstrikes have killed or injured children since the 2021 coup — with attacks on children continuing in May 2026 including the killing of five children at a Chin State playground.
footerNote: Data sourced from AAPP, ACLED, UN OCHA, Irrawaddy, RFA, Myanmar Now, DVB, Al Jazeera, Mizzima, Human Rights Watch, Crisis Group, Myanmar Peace Monitor, MoeMaKa CDM News, IMNA / Mon News Agency, CPJ, Narinjara News, Global Arakan Network, Kachin Human Rights Watch, Aryan Age, NUG Ministry of Human Rights, Committee to Protect Journalists, Chin People's Union and Army (CPU/A), Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK), IIMM (UN Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar), and official NUG, KNU, KIA, AA, and PDF statements.
